section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Bernoulli Trials
section_1.content: Define a 'Bernoulli Trial' as a single experiment with exactly two outcomes: Success (p) or Failure (1-p). Visualize this as a simple coin flip animation: Head (Success) vs. Tail (Failure).
section_1.example: Flipping a fair coin: Head (Success, p=0.5), Tail (Failure, q=0.5).

section_2.title: Defining the Binomial Conditions (BINS)
section_2.content: Introduce the BINS mnemonic: Binary (two outcomes), Independent (trials don't affect each other), Number (fixed number of trials 'n'), Success (constant probability 'p'). Use a checklist visual to emphasize these constraints.
section_2.example: A basketball player shooting 10 free throws; each shot is independent with a fixed 70% success rate.

section_3.title: The Binomial Formula Breakdown
section_3.content: Explain the formula: P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Break it down visually: C(n,k) represents the number of ways to arrange successes, while p^k * (1-p)^(n-k) represents the probability of a specific sequence.
section_3.example: Using the combination tree: Calculating the probability of getting exactly 2 heads in 3 tosses.

section_4.title: Visualizing the Probability Distribution
section_4.content: Display a dynamic bar chart that changes shape as 'n' and 'p' parameters are adjusted. Show how the distribution shifts and becomes more symmetric as 'n' increases (Central Limit Theorem hint).
section_4.example: Animation showing 5, 10, and 20 tosses; watch the 'bell curve' shape emerge for 100 trials.

section_5.title: Real-World Application: Quality Control
section_5.content: Apply the concept to a factory scenario. Calculate the probability of having 'k' defective devices in a batch to demonstrate how companies use this to maintain quality standards.
section_5.example: A robot arm on an assembly line has a 2% defect rate. Calculate the probability of finding exactly 1 defective unit in a batch of 50.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.2 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Probability Distribution", [
            "Bar charts visualize binomial distributions.",
            "Adjust parameters n and p.",
            "Symmetry increases as n grows."
        ])

        # Binomial distribution utility
        from scipy.stats import binom

        def get_bar_chart(n, p):
            x = np.arange(0, n + 1)
            y = binom.pmf(x, n, p)
            bars = VGroup(*[
                Rectangle(height=y_val * 4, width=0.8 / (n + 1), color=BLUE_B, fill_opacity=0.7)
                for y_val in y
            ])
            bars.arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge=DOWN, buff=0.1)
            return bars

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE_B))
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 1, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 1], x_length=4, y_length=3).shift(self.grid["C3"])
        self.play(Create(axes))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW_A))
        
        chart1 = get_bar_chart(5, 0.5).move_to(axes.get_center())
        chart2 = get_bar_chart(10, 0.5).move_to(axes.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(chart1))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Transform(chart1, chart2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN_A))
